label: Upper Austria: split ⇄ joins Vienna-Danube corridor

views.label: Upper Austria joins the Vienna-Danube corridor
views.note: Models the real Vienna-Linz Danube-valley rail/river economic axis by merging at-upper-austria into at-vienna-east's territory (at-vienna-danube-extended); this is an alternative economic-geography framing, not a claim that Upper Austrians identify primarily with Vienna.

views.label: Within Ostschweiz (v0.1.0 framing)
views.note: Reproduces the v0.1.0 combined framing that statistically bundled Schaffhausen into the broad Zentral-/Ostschweiz macro-region, kept available as a toggle rather than deleted outright.

label: Bremen ⇄ Lower Saxony: together / split / united

views.label: Together (current default: Bremen and Lower Saxony as separate Länder)
Lower Saxony split (west / east around Bremen)
views.note: West = Weser-Ems (Oldenburg/Cloppenburg/East Frisia, urban core Oldenburg); East = Braunschweig+Hannover+Lüneburg, urban core Hannover.

views.label: Lower Saxony united (Bremen enclave absorbed)
views.note: Reflects Bremen's historical origin as a Lower-Saxon Hanseatic city and its complete geographic enclosure by Lower Saxony; the default map keeps Bremen as its own sovereign city-state Land.

views.label: Overlapping claims
views.note: Demonstrates Bremen's enclave status within Lower Saxony's territory. This variant set merges the plan's separately named 'lower-saxony' and 'bremen' mandates into one set (4 views) because both would otherwise toggle visibility on the same underlying de-lower-saxony/de-bremen records, producing conflicting view states if kept as two independent sets -- documented in zone1.json's notes.
